title: Apophis 2029: what a kinetic impactor buys, and how far ahead the miss can be guaranteed
description: The momentum enhancement the published DART period change implies (the model is held to the mission that flew it), the miss distance at the 2029-04-13 Apophis flyby against impactor mass and warning time, and an ensemble over beta and the Yarkovsky A2 that turns the two into a success fraction and a trust horizon. The propagator is the one the repository ships (Sun, planets, Moon, the Sun's relativistic term, DE421) started from the bundled JPL osculating elements, and the encounter it produces is compared with the published one.

metrics.name: beta_recovered_from_dart
metrics.how: dart_beta() from the published 570 kg at 6.1 km/s and the 32-min period change of Dimorphos around Didymos; the published value is 3.61

metrics.name: period_change_implied_minutes
metrics.how: delta_v with the recovered beta fed back through dP/P = 3 dv/v on the 11.92 h orbit; published -32 +/- 2

metrics.name: apophis_2029_miss_km
metrics.how: closest approach to the Earth on JD 2462240.41 (2029-04-13) from the bundled JPL elements, 7.41 km/s relative; 0.000256 au

metrics.name: apophis_miss_1000kg_5yr_km
metrics.how: the same encounter after a 1000 kg impactor 5 years earlier (0.408 mm/s): +204 km on the undeflected miss

metrics.name: apophis_miss_10000kg_10yr_km
metrics.how: 10 000 kg 10 years earlier (4.078 mm/s): +2 409 km -- the heaviest case in the table, still a fraction of the Earth's radius

metrics.name: what_if_50m_miss_1000kg_5yr_km
metrics.how: the same impulse on a 50 m body (1.3e8 kg) on the same orbit: 169 mm/s and +87 000 km, i.e. a miss guaranteed by the deflection itself

metrics.name: ensemble_spread_10yr_km
metrics.how: standard deviation of the miss over 6 draws of beta (sigma 0.35) and Yarkovsky A2 (sigma 3e-15 au/day^2) at 10 years; the Earth's radius is 6 371 km

metrics.name: success_probability_10yr
metrics.how: fraction of the ensemble further from the Earth than its radius at 10 years (1.00 at 1, 5 and 10 years)

checks.name: the encounter the propagator produces against the published one
checks.detail: 38 356 km / 7.41 km/s against the ~31 000 km of the published solution: 20 %, the 16 perturbing asteroids this field does not carry

references: JPL Small-Body Database: 99942 Apophis elements (the bundled record, public domain)
DART / Dimorphos: 570 kg at 6.1 km/s, period change 32 +/- 2 min, beta = 3.61 (NASA/APL published results)
